cards.front: The ESETT trial found second-line agents for status epilepticus (levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, valproate) were equally effective, each terminating seizures ~[___]% of the time.
cards.context:
ESETT (NEJM 2019) compared the three commonly-used second-line anti-seizure medications for benzodiazepine-resistant status: levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, valproate.

So the choice falls to safety profile: levetiracetam — cleanest, no cardiac monitoring, fewest interactions; fosphenytoin — risk of hypotension, arrhythmias.

cards.front: Post-ROSC target SpO₂ is [___]%; hyperoxia is avoided because it increases free radical production.
cards.context:
Reperfusion after cardiac arrest is itself an injury — surviving cells face a flood of O₂ they can't fully use, generating ROS (free radicals) that damage mitochondria, membranes, DNA. Post-cardiac-arrest syndrome.

Guard: titrate FiO₂ to SpO₂ 94-98%, not 100% as 'safe default' (registries show worse neuro outcomes with hyperoxia).

cards.front: Alteplase for massive PE: [___] mg IV over 2 hours.
cards.context:
The distinction between massive, submassive, and low-risk PE determines management. Only massive PE (haemodynamic compromise) has a clear indication for systemic thrombolysis.

In cardiac arrest from PE, the 50mg bolus dose is used and CPR must continue for at least 60-90 minutes post-lysis to allow the drug to work.

cards.front: First-line vasopressor in septic shock: [___]. If inadequate response, add vasopressin (works via V1 receptors).
cards.context:
Catecholamine alpha-1 receptors become progressively desensitised after prolonged high-dose stimulation, so escalating a single agent eventually plateaus on MAP.

Adding a non-catecholamine that acts through V1 receptors (vasopressin) restores tone via a parallel pathway, and lets the noradrenaline dose come down.

cards.front: Under PACSA, a single normal troponin allows safe discharge only if symptoms resolved >[___] before the blood draw.
cards.context:
The Australasian Chest Pain Algorithm (PACSA) uses high-sensitivity troponin to risk-stratify ED chest pain.

If symptoms are recent (<6 h), either repeat the troponin at 1-3 h (according to the local accelerated protocol) or admit for serial sampling.

cards.front: In haemodynamically stable paroxysmal AF, the initial approach is [___] control and treating the underlying precipitant.
cards.context:
Stable paroxysmal AF in a hospitalised patient is almost always *secondary* — sepsis, pulmonary embolism, hyperthyroidism, acute pulmonary oedema, electrolyte disturbance (low K, low Mg), pain, alcohol withdrawal.

So the framing flips: don't focus on cardioverting the rhythm; control the rate (β-blocker, diltiazem, digoxin if HF) AND treat the trigger (antibiotics for sepsis, anticoagulant for PE, etc.).

cards.front: Before emergency surgery in shock: correct coagulopathy and optimise [___] with vasopressors (15-30 min resuscitation).
cards.context:
The 15-30 minute window before knife-to-skin is the highest-yield window in the whole admission.

The patient who arrives in theatre with MAP 50 and INR 2.4 will lose more on the table than they had to, and intraoperative correction always lags behind ongoing loss.

cards.front: An ICU patient on prolonged high-dose propofol develops metabolic acidosis, rising CK, and bradycardia. This syndrome is called [___].
cards.context:
Propofol's lipid vehicle causes vasodilation (hypotension). It's metabolized to green quinol derivatives (green urine in PRIS).

PRIS features: metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalaemia, cardiac failure, and lipemia.

cards.front: EpiPen Jr (150 mcg) can be used from [___] kg; adult 300 mcg device from 20 kg; 500 mcg device from 50 kg.
cards.context: 150 mcg autoinjectors (EpiPen Jr, Anapen Jr) can be used in children over 7.5 kg. This is important for discharge planning and parent education.

cards.front: Propofol infusion syndrome causes Type B lactic acidosis via [___] toxicity, with classic elevated CK.
cards.context:
PRIS (propofol infusion syndrome) is a rare but lethal complication of high-dose, prolonged propofol — historically associated with rates >4 mg/kg/hr for >48 hours, but described at lower doses.

The clinical syndrome: unexplained metabolic acidosis + rhabdomyolysis (CK ↑↑) + ARF + arrhythmia + cardiogenic shock + green-tinged urine (rare but characteristic).

cards.front: 2.5 L of normal saline delivers [___] mmol of sodium per day — well above the Holliday-Segar maintenance target. NS, Hartmann's, and Plasmalyte are all classed as replacement fluids, not maintenance fluids.
cards.context:
Normal saline delivers 154 mmol Na/L; 2.5 L/day gives 385 mmol Na — over 5× the Holliday-Segar maintenance target of 75 mmol.

Hartmann's (131 mmol/L) and Plasmalyte (140 mmol/L) are similarly excessive.

These solutions are designed to replace acute losses, not to maintain a fasting patient.

cards.front: VBG-to-ABG conversion: arterial pH is approximately 0.03 higher than venous, and arterial pCO₂ is [___] mmHg lower.
cards.context:
The VBG-to-ABG difference comes from venous CO₂ accumulation in tissues. pH is consistently ~0.03 higher arterially; pCO₂ is 3-8 mmHg lower arterially.

VBG is reliable for pH, pCO₂, HCO₃⁻, and lactate trending in most ICU contexts; ABG remains needed when accurate PaO₂ is required (oxygenation assessment.

cards.front: Inotrope increases myocardial contractility, vasopressor causes [___], and chronotrope changes heart rate.
cards.context: Use IVC to decode cardiovascular drug actions quickly under pressure.

cards.front: Normal ABG: pH [___], pCO₂ 35–45 mmHg, HCO₃ 22–26 mmol/L.
cards.context:
Anchor on 7.4 / 40 / 24. VBG offsets: pH ~0.03 lower, pCO₂ ~6 higher, HCO₃ same.

VBG cannot assess PaO₂.

cards.front: The cornerstone of delirium management is treating the [___] cause (not antipsychotics).
cards.context:
There is no effective pharmacotherapy for delirium itself. Antipsychotics do not improve outcomes — they may convert hyperactive to hypoactive delirium, making the patient 'easier to manage' but not better.

The only effective treatment is identifying and reversing the underlying cause.

cards.front: Clopidogrel in STEMI fibrinolysis: give a [___] mg loading dose in adults up to 75; in those over 75 omit the loading dose and start 75 mg daily.
cards.context:
Patients over 75 have higher ICH/bleeding risk with fibrinolysis, so the clopidogrel loading dose is skipped and maintenance (75 mg daily) is started directly — it is not a reduced loading dose.

Confirm the exact age cut-off against your local pathway.

cards.front: Earliest sign of opioid toxicity is sedation (before respiratory depression). Titrate naloxone to [___], not full alertness.
cards.context: Sedation appears before respiratory depression — it's the warning sign to act on. Titrate naloxone gently to restore breathing (not full consciousness) to avoid precipitating acute withdrawal and agitation.

cards.front: Post-arrest ABG targets? SpO₂: 94–98% (avoid hyperoxia). PaCO₂: 35–45 mmHg (normocapnia). Acidosis: treat the [___], not pH (bicarb only if pH < 7.1).
cards.context:
Post-ROSC hyperoxia worsens neurological outcomes via free radical injury. Hypocapnia reduces cerebral perfusion; hypercapnia increases ICP.

Bicarbonate generates CO₂ — rarely indicated unless pH below 7.1.

cards.front: The ESETT trial found second-line agents for status epilepticus (levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, valproate) were [___] effective, each terminating seizures ~45-50% of the time.
cards.context:
ESETT (NEJM 2019) compared the three commonly-used second-line anti-seizure medications for benzodiazepine-resistant status: levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, valproate.

So the choice falls to safety profile: levetiracetam — cleanest, no cardiac monitoring, fewest interactions; fosphenytoin — risk of hypotension, arrhythmias.

cards.front: Vasopressin in septic shock is given at a fixed dose of [___] units/min and is not titrated.
cards.context:
Vasopressin is added when noradrenaline alone fails to reach MAP target (typically once nor exceeds 0.25-0.5 mcg/kg/min).

It is NOT titrated to effect because higher doses cause splanchnic, coronary, and digital ischaemia without proportional MAP gain — a fixed sub-pressor dose is the safe sweet spot.

cards.front: Delta ratio: (AG − 12) / (24 − [___]). A ratio '<'1 suggests concurrent NAGMA; '>'2 suggests concurrent metabolic alkalosis.
cards.context:
Delta ratio = (AG − 12) / (24 − HCO₃). Detects second metabolic disorders hidden by HAGMA.

A pure HAGMA has 1:1 relationship between AG rise and HCO₃ fall. Ratio <1 = concurrent NAGMA; 1-2 = pure HAGMA; >2 = concurrent metabolic alkalosis.

cards.front: Septic shock (Sepsis-3): vasopressors needed for MAP ≥65 mmHg AND lactate >[___] mmol/L despite adequate fluids.
cards.context:
Sepsis-3 defines septic shock as sepsis with persistent hypotension requiring vasopressors AND lactate >2 despite adequate fluids. Both criteria must be met.

This subset carries >40% mortality.

cards.front: Refractory shock: noradrenaline >[___] mcg/kg/min. Add vasopressin and hydrocortisone, reassess for missed pathology.
cards.context: Rising vasopressor doses signal either inadequate source control, ongoing losses, or refractory vasodilation.

cards.front: Exercise-associated hyponatraemia (EAH) risk factors include slow pace, female sex, low body weight, excessive fluid intake, [___] use, and race duration >4 hours.
cards.context: EAH risk factors are clinically important because you can counsel athletes before the race. Slow runners spend more time drinking; NSAIDs impair renal free water clearance; smaller athletes dilute faster.

cards.front: A >[___] mmHg blood pressure difference between arms suggests aortic dissection.
cards.context:
Inter-arm SBP difference >20 mmHg is one of the bedside flags for aortic dissection — the dissection flap can occlude flow into the brachiocephalic or left subclavian, depending on the entry point.

It's not sensitive (~30%) but is reasonably specific (~85%). Combine with the other dissection signs: tearing chest/back pain, unequal pulses, neurological deficit (carotid involvement), widened mediastinum on CXR.

cards.front: The initial aspirin dose in suspected ACS is [___] mg, administered by chewing or dissolving.
cards.context:
Aspirin 300 mg loading dose blocks platelet COX-1 within 15-30 minutes — chewing or dissolving accelerates absorption vs swallowed enteric-coated.

Maintenance is 100 mg/day. Contraindications: active GI bleeding, true aspirin allergy. The benefit applies even before STEMI/NSTEMI is confirmed — give to anyone with credible suspected ACS unless contraindicated.

cards.front: Ottawa Ankle Rules: X-ray if tenderness at posterior [___] or medial malleolus (distal 6 cm), base of 5th metatarsal, navicular bone, or unable to weight-bear 4 steps.
cards.context: The Ottawa rules check four bony areas plus weight-bearing ability. The midfoot component (base of 5th MT and navicular) is often forgotten but catches important fractures that can be missed clinically.

cards.front: First-line treatment for anaphylaxis is IM adrenaline [___] mg into the anterolateral thigh.
cards.context:
Anaphylaxis is histamine-driven distributive shock + airway oedema + bronchoconstriction — kills via airway loss or CV collapse within minutes.

IM lateral thigh gives faster, more reliable absorption than deltoid, avoiding IV-bolus risks. Dose 0.5 mg adult, 0.01 mg/kg paediatric (max 0.5), repeat q5min.

cards.front: DSM-5 criterion E requires delirium to have a direct [___] cause (not psychiatric).
cards.context: Delirium does NOT occur in the context of coma (severely reduced arousal) and is NOT a psychiatric illness. There must always be an identifiable organic cause — infection, substance, metabolic derangement, etc.

cards.front: During massive transfusion protocol (MTP), hypocalcaemia from citrate toxicity causes hypotension and prolonged QT. Treat with IV [___].
cards.context:
Stored blood is anticoagulated with citrate; normal volumes clear within minutes, but in MTP the load outstrips clearance and citrate binds free ionised calcium — sometimes precipitously.

Check iCa (not total — only the ionised fraction is active) every 4-6 units PRBCs in MTP; replace with 10 mL of 10% calcium gluconate IV (or CaCl₂ centrally) for symptoms or iCa <1.0 mmol/L.

cards.front: Australian meningitis empiric: ceftriaxone 2 g IV 12-hourly + [___] 10 mg IV; add ampicillin if Listeria risk.
cards.context:
Australian eTG diverges from US guidelines: ceftriaxone alone covers the dominant pathogens (Strep pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis) without routinely adding vancomycin.

Listeria is the trap.

US guidelines also add vancomycin routinely; for the AU exam, follow eTG.

cards.front: First-line treatment in anaphylaxis is [___] adrenaline using the 1:1000 concentration.
cards.context:
IM adrenaline 1:1000 (1 mg/mL) is the only intervention that addresses *all* features of anaphylaxis simultaneously: α-1 vasoconstriction reverses hypotension and mucosal oedema.

The IM anterolateral thigh route gives faster, more reliable absorption than deltoid even in shock.

cards.front: The most specific ECG finding for severe hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >7.5 mmol/L, normal 3.5-5.0) is a [___] pattern.
cards.context:
Hyperkalaemia progressively destabilises the cardiac action potential as K⁺ rises: peaked T waves (5.5-6.5) → PR prolongation and P-wave flattening (6.5-7.5) → QRS widening (>7.5)

This is one of the few ECG patterns where the rhythm tells you the chemistry; treat the K⁺ aggressively (calcium → insulin/dex → salbutamol → resonium → dialysis).

cards.front: Delta ratio: (AG − 12) / (24 − HCO₃). A ratio '<'1 suggests concurrent NAGMA; '>'2 suggests concurrent [___].
cards.context:
Delta ratio = (AG − 12) / (24 − HCO₃). Detects second metabolic disorders hidden by HAGMA.

A pure HAGMA has 1:1 relationship between AG rise and HCO₃ fall. Ratio <1 = concurrent NAGMA; 1-2 = pure HAGMA; >2 = concurrent metabolic alkalosis.

cards.front: A non-rebreather has a [___] bag and one-way valves to reduce re-breathing and room air entrainment. Max FiO₂: 60-80%.
cards.context: Side ports with partial one-way valves reduce room air entrainment during inspiration. Despite this, they still only achieve 60-80% FiO₂ because they're variable performance.

cards.front: Analgesic-dose ketamine (approximately 0.1 mg/kg) is notable for preserving [___] drive, unlike opioids.
cards.context:
At sub-anaesthetic analgesic doses (approximately 0.1 mg/kg IV), ketamine preserves airway reflexes and respiratory drive.

Rare side effects at low dose include salivation and dysphoria.

cards.front: Post-arrest ABG targets? SpO₂: 94–98% (avoid hyperoxia). PaCO₂: [___] mmHg (normocapnia). Acidosis: treat the cause, not pH (bicarb only if pH < 7.1).
cards.context:
Post-ROSC hyperoxia worsens neurological outcomes via free radical injury. Hypocapnia reduces cerebral perfusion; hypercapnia increases ICP.

Bicarbonate generates CO₂ — rarely indicated unless pH below 7.1.

cards.front: Delta ratio setup: delta anion gap = measured AG minus 12; delta bicarbonate = [___] minus measured bicarbonate.
cards.context:
Delta ratio = ΔAG ÷ ΔHCO₃⁻. ΔAG = measured AG minus normal AG (12). ΔHCO₃⁻ = normal HCO₃⁻ (24) minus measured HCO₃⁻.

Interpretation: <0.4 = pure normal AG acidosis; 0.4-0.8 = mixed high AG + normal AG acidosis; 0.8-2.0 = pure high AG acidosis; >2.0 = high AG acidosis + concurrent metabolic alkalosis.

cards.front: The most specific Sgarbossa criterion for STEMI in LBBB is concordant ST elevation of at least [___] in any lead.
cards.context:
Sgarbossa identifies STEMI on top of LBBB. LBBB normally has discordant ST changes — Sgarbossa flags the patterns that signal ischaemia.

Most specific finding is ST elevation that goes WITH the dominant QRS direction (rather than against it as expected in LBBB).

cards.front: Post-ROSC, target SpO₂ [___]% to avoid hyperoxia, which worsens neurological outcomes via free radical injury.
cards.context:
Post-ROSC the brain is in a vulnerable reperfusion state — every excess oxygen molecule generates reactive oxygen species (superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, hydroxyl radical) that compound the original ischaemic injury.

SpO₂ 94-98% (titrate FiO₂ down from 1.0 once SpO₂ confirmed reliable) is the post-arrest standard. Same principle applies to neonatal resus: use room air or low FiO₂, escalate only if SpO₂ targets are missed.

cards.front: Heart rate from a regular ECG: rate = [___] divided by the number of large boxes between R waves.
cards.context:
ECG paper at standard speed runs 25 mm/s, so each large box (5 mm) is 0.2 seconds. Five large boxes = 1 second; 300 large boxes = 1 minute (300 × 0.2 s = 60 s).

Useful memorised landmarks: 1 box = 300/min, 2 = 150, 3 = 100, 4 = 75, 5 = 60, 6 = 50. Only valid for regular rhythms — for irregular rhythms (e.g., AF) count R waves in the 10-second strip and multiply by 6.

cards.front: Massive transfusion is defined as replacement of the entire blood volume in [___] hours or half in 4 hours.
cards.context: Massive transfusion has two definitions: replacement of the entire blood volume in 24 hours, OR half the blood volume in 4 hours.

cards.front: Normal anion gap range is [___].
cards.context: The anion gap represents unmeasured anions (albumin, phosphate, lactate, ketones, toxins). Hypoalbuminaemia lowers the gap by ~2.5 per 10 g/L albumin drop.
